title: Brake Testing
body: A truck that can't stop on a loaded ramp is the fastest way to lose someone at ADW. The pre-shift brake test is the one control that catches a failing machine before it ever carries a load into the pit — skip it or wave it through and you're gambling on the highwall and the queue behind it.
keyPoints: Every surface mobile machine gets tested before shift — trucks, ADTs, water carts, graders, dozers, loaders, LDVs. No exceptions; anything unusual gets a risk-based call, not a pass.
Two checks, in order: the operator's own pull-away-and-stop check right after pre-use inspection, then the brake test ramp for structured verification.
On the ramp: dead stop on the incline using service brake, dead stop on the decline, then park brake test. "Slows down" is not "dead stop" — a soft stop is a fail.
A failed test is one path only: park immediately, lock out (LOTO), notify supervisor or Maintenance. No "finish the shift and we'll look at it."
Repeat failures on the same unit aren't a nuisance — they're a signal that unit needs a deeper service intervention, not another retest.
apply: On your morning walk, stand at the brake test ramp for a few minutes — the queue, how operators run the test, and whether anyone rolls past it tells you more about shift-start discipline than any report will.
